purpose: Per-machine hold rules. A hold is scored differently depending on whether the muscle is still loaded in that position or the load has been taken off it. Without this every pause is judged the same way, which penalises a client for holding a loaded contraction and lets a rest at the bottom pass.
classificationTest: Put the machine in the hold position and ask: if the client completely relaxed right now, would the stack move? If it drops, the muscle was holding it -> LOADED. If nothing happens, the skeleton or the resting plates are taking the load -> REST.

rules.LOADED: The hold is work. Scored one-sided, like a contraction: holding longer than target is free, cutting it short deducts.
rules.REST: The hold is dead time. Holding longer than target deducts.

positions.top: Stack raised. Always the end of the concentric and the muscle at its shortest, whichever way the client's limb travelled.
positions.bottom: Stack down. Start position, muscle at its longest. Coached as a HOVER throughout, so the plates stay off the stack and the muscle keeps holding the load — LOADED by default. Setting the plates down would release tension and make it REST.

machines.name: Leg Extension
machines.notes: Knee cannot lock out and shed load to the skeleton, so the quad holds the leg against the pad through full extension. Bottom is a coached hover, so the quad keeps holding the load in the stretched position.

machines.name: Leg Curl
machines.notes: Hamstring holds the pad against resistance at full knee flexion, with no position the skeleton can take over. Bottom is a coached hover, so the hamstring keeps holding the load in the stretched position.

machines.name: Leg Curl (seated)
machines.notes: Hamstring holds against resistance at full flexion. Bottom set to LOADED by the coached-hover policy — submitted as REST, which would only be right if this machine's bottom position sheds the load even when hovered. Confirm.

machines.name: Tibialis Dorsi Flexion
machines.notes: Bottom set to LOADED by the coached-hover policy. Small joint through a small range, so stack travel is likely to be the shortest in the estate — tape it and check the signal ratio before relying on this one. May only be viable at a quicker tempo.

machines.name: Leg Press
machines.notes: First machine where the two ends differ. At the top the knees lock and the load passes through the skeleton, so holding there is rest however it is coached — the hover policy does not override it. At the bottom the knees are flexed and the quads hold the carriage, so the hover is work. Often geared 2:1 to keep the stack manageable, which would halve the travel the phone sees — worth taping.

coaching.note: Clients are always coached to hover at the bottom rather than set the plates down. A hovered stack stays suspended, so the muscle is still holding it and the bottom hold is LOADED by default across the estate. A machine only overrides this if its own bottom position genuinely sheds the load.
